story.title: Harvey Weinstein Receives 15-Year Sentence for 2006 Sexual Assault
story.summary: Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting Miriam Haley in 2006. This sentencing follows a lengthy legal process that included a retrial, where a jury found him guilty of the charges. The sentencing took place in New York.

explore_lenses.label: How did Weinstein’s case reach this sentence?
explore_lenses.title: A conviction was overturned, then partly rebuilt
explore_lenses.summary: The 15-year sentence follows a retrial process set in motion when New York’s highest court vacated Weinstein’s 2020 conviction and 23-year sentence. The later proceedings produced a new conviction involving Miriam Haley, while related allegations ended differently.

claims.text: In April 2024, the New York Court of Appeals ordered a new trial, finding that the original trial improperly admitted testimony about uncharged alleged acts and allowed potentially prejudicial cross-examination about misconduct.

A Manhattan jury convicted Weinstein on June 11, 2025, of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Miriam Haley; the jury acquitted him on a separate allegation and could not reach a verdict on the Jessica Mann rape count.

After a subsequent mistrial on the Mann count, Manhattan prosecutors said in June 2026 that they would consider their next steps in consultation with Mann and in light of the pending Haley sentencing; the rape charge was later dropped rather than tried a fourth time.

After a subsequent mistrial on the Mann count, Manhattan prosecutors said in June 2026 that they would consider their next steps in consultation with Mann and in light of the pending Haley sentencing; the rape charge was later dropped rather than tried a fourth time.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The sentence concerns the Haley conviction, not every allegation raised across Weinstein’s New York trials.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the 15-year term matter?
explore_lenses.title: It replaces the voided New York punishment
explore_lenses.summary: The new sentence establishes punishment for the one New York felony conviction that remained after the retrial sequence. It does not restore the 2020 judgment, which was entirely vacated.

claims.text: The 2020 New York judgment had imposed 23 years for convictions involving Haley and Mann, but the Court of Appeals reversed that judgment and ordered a new trial.
The first-degree criminal-sex-act count involving Haley carried a maximum possible New York sentence of 25 years; before sentencing, prosecutors had sought a 20-year term.

Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg characterized the 2025 verdict as accountability for Haley and thanked her for testifying again; Weinstein has denied sexually assaulting or raping anyone, and his defense has argued that the proceedings were unfair.

explore_lenses.label: What legal proceedings remain?
explore_lenses.title: California resentencing and appeals remain open
explore_lenses.summary: The New York sentencing does not end Weinstein’s separate California criminal case. California’s appellate courts have upheld his conviction but required resentencing, and his lawyers have sought review by the state Supreme Court.

claims.text: A California appeals court in June 2026 affirmed Weinstein’s 2022 Los Angeles convictions but vacated his 16-year sentence and remanded the case for resentencing.
California appellate records show that Weinstein filed a petition for review in the California Supreme Court on August 5, 2026.
Weinstein’s lawyers have also challenged the 2025 New York conviction, alleging juror intimidation and outside bias; those allegations were arguments by the defense, not findings of misconduct.

story_report.summary: Harvey Weinstein was sentenced in New York to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting Miriam Haley in 2006, following a retrial after his earlier New York judgment was overturned. The sentence applies to the conviction involving Haley and follows a legal process that has included multiple proceedings over allegations involving other women. It imposes a new prison term on the first-degree criminal-sex-act conviction returned by a Manhattan jury in 2025.

sections.heading: New York Retrial Followed Reversal
sections.body: Weinstein’s original 2020 New York judgment imposed a 23-year sentence on convictions involving Haley and Jessica Mann. In April 2024, New York’s highest court reversed that judgment and ordered a new trial, finding that the first trial had improperly admitted testimony concerning uncharged alleged acts and permitted potentially prejudicial cross-examination. At the retrial, a Manhattan jury convicted Weinstein on June 11, 2025, of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley.

sections.heading: Haley Conviction Defines New Sentence
sections.body: The 15-year term concerns the Haley conviction rather than all allegations raised during Weinstein’s New York cases. The count carried a maximum possible sentence of 25 years, and prosecutors had sought 20 years before sentencing. In the 2025 retrial, the jury acquitted Weinstein on a separate allegation and did not reach a verdict on the Mann rape count; after a later mistrial on that count, prosecutors ultimately dropped the rape charge rather than try it a fourth time.

sections.heading: Weinstein Challenges New York Proceedings
sections.body: Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg described the 2025 verdict as accountability for Haley and thanked her for testifying again. Weinstein has denied sexually assaulting or raping anyone, while his defense has argued that the proceedings were unfair. His lawyers have also challenged the 2025 New York conviction by alleging juror intimidation and outside bias; those assertions are defense arguments, not findings of misconduct.

unresolved.text: It remains unresolved whether New York appellate litigation will alter Weinstein’s new conviction or 15-year sentence.

The time Weinstein will ultimately remain incarcerated depends on sentence-credit calculations and continuing litigation in New York and California. California’s appellate court affirmed his 2022 Los Angeles convictions but vacated the 16-year sentence for resentencing, and he has petitioned the California Supreme Court for review.

related_stories.title: Hurricane Polo Reaches Category 5 Status Off Mexico's Pacific Coast
related_stories.summary: Hurricane Polo has intensified into one of the strongest storms ever recorded in the Pacific, reaching Category 5 status with maximum sustained winds exceeding 157 mph (253 kph). The storm is currently off the southwestern coast of Mexico and is being influenced by warm waters associated with the El Niño phenomenon. Although it has since weakened to a Category 4 storm, it remains a powerful cyclone expected to affect the region.

related_stories.title: Mass Shooting at South African House Party Claims 11 Lives
related_stories.summary: A mass shooting at a house party in South Africa resulted in the deaths of at least 11 people, including a pregnant woman. The attack involved three gunmen who forced the victims into a single room before opening fire, leaving only two survivors. Police are currently searching for the attackers.

related_stories.title: Morocco Holds Parliamentary Elections Amid Youth Discontent and Economic Concerns
related_stories.summary: Moroccans are voting in parliamentary elections today, with significant concerns regarding the cost of living, jobs, and inequality. Many voters, particularly the youth, express deep distrust in political parties, reflecting a broader discontent that has been evident since youth-led demonstrations a year ago. The elections are seen as a crucial test of citizens' faith in the political process as the country prepares for the 2030 World Cup.

related_stories.title: Tigray Forces Capture Airports Amid Renewed Fighting in Ethiopia
related_stories.summary: Tigrayan rebels have taken control of airports in northern Ethiopia and engaged in clashes with federal troops in the Afar region. This escalation marks a significant resurgence of conflict, with reports indicating that Ethiopian Airlines has suspended flights to three airports in Tigray, signaling a breakdown of the Pretoria Agreement that had previously ended the 2020-2022 war.
